subject: Request: short-term dedicated pool window for Nimbus pilot
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term dedicated pool window for Nimbus pilot

Team —

We have a timeboxed pilot with Nimbus Labs that just moved up to the first week of June. They expect steady inference traffic across a 4-day window (Mon–Thu, 7–10 June is their preferred run but will accept 7–10 June; updated note below). This is a production-facing evaluation and Nimbus asked for a guaranteed dedicated slice to remove eviction risk during their demo runs.

Quick summary:
- What: short-term dedicated carve for pilot (GPU pool reservation + autoscale exception)
- When: proposal to reserve capacity June 6 evening preload + June 7–10 daily window 08:00–20:00 PT
- Size ask: equivalent of 4 x A100-80GB (we can express as 4 gpus or 2 large nodes depending on topology)
- Why: consistent tail latency during multi-tenant peak for demo and small stress tests; the customer will judge latency and throughput directly in their procurement committee

Asks:
1) Can infra / capacity make a temporary carve that prevents soft-eviction for that window (we're OK with a hard budget cap)?
2) Product: confirm SLO/throughput targets we need to guarantee (latency P95 target, ops/sec) so we can include in the pilot MOP and commercial term.
3) Sales/Commercial (Dev): do we have flexibility on billing (one-off reservation fee + usage) and can we commit to the proposed window if infra needs a smaller footprint?

Attachments: nimbus_pilot_mop.pdf, pilot_sla_request.xlsx (draft SLA the customer sent).

I know we have other pilots in the same timeframe — I listed Laura and Marcus to coordinate tradeoffs. Happy to take this to a quick 30-min sync if useful.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term dedicated pool window for Nimbus pilot

Thanks Grace — useful context. A few clarifying questions before infra sizes a carve:

1) SLAs: the attached SLA requests 95th/99th P50/P95 latency commitments and a minimum throughput target of ~120 qps (across all requests). Is that the expectation from Nimbus or is that an internal ask they sent as an aspirational MOP? We need to be precise: product can sign up to a P95 latency target for the pilot only if the configuration is dedicated and the tokenization/seq lengths are bounded.

2) Workload profile: are we seeing short prompt/response pairs (<= 512 tokens) or long generations? If they plan long-generated responses we need to account for KV-cache growth and elevated memory pressure.

3) Fallback behavior: product prefers we leave a fallback route to an on-host model variant (lower-capacity quantized) rather than total blocking the customer if something goes wrong. If infra disables soft-eviction entirely we need an explicit fallback policy.

If we can get minute-level QPS forecast for the 4-day window (peak QPS each hour + expected seq lengths), I can finalize the P95 commitment we can make in the SLA. Happy to take a 20-min handoff with Marcus to align.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: short-term dedicated pool window for Nimbus pilot

Quick infra readout and a proposed config. TL;DR — we can satisfy a short carve with conditions below.

Current constraints:
- Pool utilization for week-of-6 June is forecasted at ~76% across existing reservations and expected autoscale bursts. We have two enterprise pilots (X and Y) with scheduled load in overlapping days; both are lower priority than Nimbus but have committed reservations (can't evict their reserved slices).
- Autoscaler: default behavior is to allow soft-eviction of on-demand slices during contention. Turning soft-eviction off for a window is possible but means we must set a hard reserve limit and cap total usage to protect other commitments.

Proposed carve (config attached as proposed_carve_config.json):
- Reserve: 3 x A100-80GB equivalent dedicated (we can expand to 4 if product signs off on exact token/seq forecasts)
- Window: preload 2027-06-06 20:00 PT (image/model warm) + active window 2027-06-07 08:00–2027-06-10 20:00 PT
- Autoscale exception: disable soft-eviction within the reserved allocation but apply a spend cap of $X/day (we'll provide estimate below)
- Fallback: allow routing to a quantized fallback model in a separate pool if customer traffic exceeds reserved throughput, but routing requires explicit product opt-in (to avoid violating demo expectations)

Estimated cost delta to run reserve vs on-demand for 4 days: approx $17,200 (this includes preload costs and a 20% ops buffer). If we shrink to 3 GPUs the delta drops to ~$12,900.

Impact:
- If we commit to 3 gpus, we can honor all other reservations; committing to 4 will require temporary re-scheduling of one background test early morning slot on June 8 (we can coordinate with owners).

Next steps:
- Kim: confirm P95 target and tokens/seq to lock size (3 vs 4)
- Dev: confirm commercial approval for the estimated reservation delta and confirm billing code
- Grace/Laura: confirm final window and any customer-facing language about fallback behavior

If everyone agrees I will provision the carve on Tue morning and run preload on Sun night.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_carve_config.json

Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term dedicated pool window for Nimbus pilot

Looping in the commercial confirmation — Nimbus and I discussed the reservation delta and they're okay to proceed with the 3-GPU carve as long as we include a clear fallback route in the pilot MOP. Nimbus confirmed they can cap prompt sequences to <= 512 tokens for the demo runs, which addresses the KV growth risk.

Commercials:
- Deal: RDW-4721 — we're approving the one-off reservation fee (use billing code RDW-PILOT-RES) and usage billed per our standard hosted usage rates for any overage outside the reserved carve.
- Nimbus has signed the MOP they sent; legal will attach the final SLA patch but product's P95 language must reflect the limited pilot duration and dedicated carve precondition.

Marcus — please proceed with provisioning the 3-GPU carve. Grace/Laura/Kim: if you can confirm the final wording for fallback (we should state: "automatic routing to quantized fallback available if reserved throughput capacity is exceeded; will be communicated to the customer before run"), infra can preload on 6 June 20:00 PT.

Tim — thanks for the quick turnaround from Nimbus. We'll send a final runbook by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
